newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Two Belgians arrested in Dassault bribe probe.
newsitem.headline: Two Belgians arrested in Dassault bribe probe.

text.p: A Belgian magistrate heading a probe into allegations the French aerospace group Dassault paid bribes to Belgian political parties has arrested two former Socialist Party officials, a court official said on Friday.
"Two warrants have been issued, the two are under arrest," a court official in Liege, eastern Belgium told Reuters.

He said investigating magistrate Jean-Louis Prignon, who heads the Dassault inquiry, had issued the warrants for Merry Hermanus and Francois Pirot, two former top officials of Belgium's francophone Socialist Party (PS).
He declined to confirm newspaper reports that the arrests were linked to the Dassault investigation. The PS was not immediately available for comment.

The Belgian judiciary is investigating claims that Dassault paid 600 million Belgian francs ($18 million) in kickbacks to Belgian political parties to secure a 1989 contract to fit air defence systems to the countries' F-16 fighter jets.
The arrests come just two weeks after a French court handed the Belgian judiciary papers relating to the Dassault probe.
In December the Dutch-speaking Christian Democratic Party CVP -- members of Belgium's coalition government along with the PS -- admitted it had been given 1.2 million francs by Dassault in 1987.
Dassault denied the company had ever made such a donation.
The Flemish Socialist Party (SP) was also reported to have received bribes from Dassault.

Last May Prignon issued an international arrest warrant for Serge Dassault, group founder and chairman of Dassault Aviation, who has denied all wrongdoing but has refused to come to Belgium to answer questions relating to the affair.
Dassault was questioned by a French court, in the presence of Belgian investigators, in Paris in November 1995.

NATO Secretary General Willy Claes, a government economics minister for the Socialist Party in the late 1980s, was forced to resign in October 1995 over bribes alleged to have been paid to his party by Dassault and Italian helicopter maker Agusta in exchange for contracts. ($1=33.78 Belgian Franc)
